anomalies.observed: On the 'MAIN PUMP & VALVE DRIVERS' sheet the two low-side switches use identical NPN common-emitter level shifters (T5 BT3904 and T1 BT3904, emitters tied to GND, collectors driving the MOSFET gate), but their gate bias resistors are tied to opposite rails: R4 (10 k) on the main-pump gate node NET0035 is pulled UP to +3V3, whereas R1 (10 k) on the ATO-valve gate is pulled DOWN to GND.
anomalies.expected: Both switches are the same intended topology (spec: T2 IRLR2905 and T3 AON6407, each 'gate driven through ... 100 Ω ... pre-driven via ... BT3904 NPN level shifter'). With a sink-only NPN pre-driver the gate needs the same bias rail on both channels; the valve's gate must be pulled up (as R4 does) so the AON6407 can ever turn on.

evidence.quote: Main Pump: R4 10k from +3V3 to NET0035 (T7 gate / T5 collector); ATO Valve: R1 10k from gate node to GND (T4 gate / T1 collector)
T2 — IRLR2905 ... gate driven through R1 (100 Ω) ... pre-driven via T1 (BT3904 NPN level shifter). T3 — AON6407 ... gate driven through R10 (100 Ω), pre-driven via T4 (BT3904).

anomalies.impact: The ATO solenoid valve (T4) cannot turn on because its gate is held at ground by R1 while the NPN level shifter can only sink; automatic top-off fails. Conversely the main circulation pump (T7) is default-ON at boot (gate pulled high when T5 is off), an unsafe/unintended state. The two otherwise-identical drivers behave inconsistently.

parsed.summary: The schematic deviates from the intended identical low-side switch design: the main-pump gate bias resistor R4 is pulled to +3V3 while the ATO-valve gate bias resistor R1 is pulled to GND, even though both use the same NPN common-emitter level shifters, leaving the valve unable to energize and the pump default-on.
